title: Using machine learning algorithms to predict MACE in peritoneal dialysis patients.
summary: Machine-learning models predicted major adverse cardiac events in a retrospective peritoneal-dialysis cohort and a separate hospital cohort. The study reports development AUCs of 0.80 overall, 0.86 at one year, and 0.75 at five years, with external-cohort AUC 0.768; its broad composite outcome and retrospective design do not establish intervention benefit.
ai_technology: XGBoost, random forest, and AdaBoost rank baseline clinical variables and predict overall, one-year, and five-year MACE risk.
organization: Second Affiliated Hospital of Xiamen Medical College; Fujian Provincial Hospital, Fujian Medical University

evidence.tested: Among 1,006 patients, 606 formed the development cohort and 400 an external hospital cohort; reported external-validation AUC was 0.768.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective data and a composite including cardiovascular hospitalization and all-cause mortality; prospective implementation and patient benefit were not tested.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning models estimate MACE risk from baseline clinical factors.

source_review.scope: Primary source full-text Methods and Results; version date and reported validation scope checked.
